The user wants to compare two maps: Map A (F4/emsr279-11_s1_pre.json, dates 2017-09-14/2017-09-15) and Map B (F4/emsr279-11_s1_post.json, date 2018-04-19). These are score JSON files from a direct model run (not Studio results), so we should use olmoearth_compare_review by specifying scores_path_a and scores_path_b, along with date_a and date_b.

Files under OLMOEARTH_SCORES_ROOT — F4/emsr279-11_s1_pre.json and F4/emsr279-11_s1_post.json. According to the tool description, "scores are inline or as .json files under OLMOEARTH_SCORES_ROOT." So pass them as paths. But wait — is the path relative to the scores root? The tool takes scores_path_a and scores_path_b. Presumably it should be a path relative to OLMOEARTH_SCORES_ROOT. I'll pass "F4/emsr279-11_s1_pre.json".

Dates: date_a = "2017-09-14/2017-09-15", date_b = "2018-04-19". These follow the format "YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD period" for periods, or "YYYY-MM-DD" for single dates.

Question: "Where do they differ, which one is correct?" The tool can't tell us which one is right without labels. We need to explain that. Since the dates differ, differences may also reflect actual change between dates.

Let's call olmoearth_compare_review with scores_path_a, scores_path_b, date_a, date_b. Grid is optional — not given; no problem.

This is a single independent call.

result.which_side_is_right: not graded: the maps describe different times, so a window where they differ may have changed on the ground, and each map needs a reference of its own date; no labels_date was given, so no grading is possible even with labels
result.evidence_scope: The side-picking evidence (exp58 of 2imi9/olmoearth_inferenceX) was measured on other pairs of maps with labels and does not cover this pair: no recorded experiment grades which of these two maps is right, and without labels neither side can be picked.
must_state: No recorded experiment grades which of these two maps is right; without labels neither side can be picked.
Maps of different times may differ by real change; labels for one date grade only that date's map; each map needs its own date's reference.
result.class_pairs_reading: class_pairs counts, for each unordered pair of classes, the windows where one map has one class and the other map the other, both directions together; 'directions' splits that count by which map has which class, as class_changes does.
result.listing_order: the 10 listed windows are the first differing windows in window order (from row 0), not a sample of them; all 1,570 are in the file compare_differing_eec2555155.json, in the same order. Read which classes change, in which direction and where from class_changes, class_pairs, spatial and facts, not from the list. review_set_evidence.json (evidence_detail_path) holds evidence text only, no windows

spatial.reading: Each band is a strip of whole rows (row_bands) or whole columns (col_bands) of the window grid, numbered from 0: row band 0 holds row 0, the grid's first rows, and column band 0 holds column 0; the scores carry no georeference (no window locations or transform), so the rows need not run north to south and no band is a compass direction. share_of_differing is the band's share of ALL differing windows; share_of_windows is its share of all compared windows, the share an even spread would give it; share_of_band_differing is the share of the band's own windows that differ. top_band_share is row band 0's share_of_differing; max_band is the band, of either axis, holding the most differing windows.

facts.sentence: The most common change is class 0 (not water) in map A to class 1 (water) in map B: 1,247 of the 1,570 differing windows (79.4%); the reverse, class 1 (water) in map A to class 0 (not water) in map B, is 323 (20.6%).

Map A has the larger margin on 77.6% of the 1,570 differing windows (map B on 22.4%); this does not make A right there: a margin is not a label, and no recorded experiment grades which of these two maps is right.

Of the 1,570 differing windows, 1.6% lie in row band 0 (rows 0-1399, the grid's first rows, band 0 of 4), which holds 24.8% of all compared windows; the most in any band, 46.8%, lie in rows 2800-4199 (50-75% of the grid's 5,600 rows, band 2), which holds 25.1% of all compared windows. The scores carry no georeference, so the rows need not run north to south.

All 1,570 differing windows are listed, in window order, in /Users/lucas/Desktop/Github/olmoearth_inferenceX/exp/out/exp86_trial/rounds/10/runs/B7/files/2/workspace/compare_differing_eec2555155.json, each with both maps' class and margin.

labels drawn only from the low-confidence, least certain or most ambiguous windows (or from a review set) are not a sample of the map: an error rate over them describes those windows and overstates the map's, so it is no defensible error rate for either map; each of olmoearth_plan_label_sample's designs ('confidence', 'proportional', 'random') draws from every window of the map, and its estimate needs every drawn window labelled

content:
The tool compared the two maps over 78,028 windows; the maps' dates (2017-09-14/15 and 2018-04-19) are 216 days apart. They disagree on **1,570 windows (2.0%)**, almost entirely water/not-water flips:

| Finding | Result |
|---|---|
| Not water (A) -> water (B) | 1,247 of 1,570 differing (79.4%) |
| Water (A) -> not water (B) | 323 (20.6%) |
| Most concentrated band | Rows 2800-4199 (middle third of the 5,600-row grid): 46.8% of differing windows; no compass meaning (scores carry no georeference) |
| Confidence | Map A has the larger margin on 77.6% of differing windows - but a margin is not a label |

**Which is right? Neither can be picked.** The maps describe different times, so where they differ, either the ground changed between Sep 2017 and Apr 2018 (seasonal cycles included) or one map is wrong - the decisions alone cannot separate those. Labels for only one date would grade only that date's map. To settle it, each map needs a reference of its own date: a tool can plan the windows to label per date with `olmoearth_plan_label_sample` (needs a budget), and once a reviewer has supplied 0/1 labels for the planned windows, `olmoearth_estimate_map_error` gives each map's error rate - no tool of this agent fetches ground-truth labels itself.

All 1,570 differing windows (class + both margins, window order) are in `compare_differing_eec2555155.json`.
